fit: pearled barley within one assigned multi-food home dinner and postprandial pressure
assessment: In spinal cord injury, home-meal maximum systolic fall showed no clear diet effect. A separate laboratory comparison did not include barley. The study did not isolate boiled barley or orthostatic lightheadedness.

fit: soybean oil in both softgel formulations and subjective swallowing adaptation
assessment: Some participants reported mild difficulty swallowing large capsules. Oil grade and arm counts were unreported. Both arms contained oil and there was no Parkinson dysphagia comparison.

fit: diet history and clinical facial signs in corticobasal degeneration
assessment: A corticobasal case had hypomimia recorded in 2013 and a later diet history naming milk and occasional chicken. No timed food exposure contrast, preparation-grade information or causally attributable facial outcome.

fit: Japanese pepper fraction with motor inhibition and altered tone in animal toxicology
assessment: The primary abstract reports lower tone preceding akinesia in one comparison and convulsions at more severe exposure. The crude constituent, animal exposure and end points do not resolve clinical rigidity after ground pepper.

fit: eugenol odor pulses during animal REM recordings
assessment: Odor produced state-sensitive cortical field-potential responses. No eugenol-specific loss-of-atonia or dream-enactment outcome was assessed and allspice was not eaten.

fit: pooled bean consumption and self-reported sleep duration or quality
assessment: The Chinese cohort found favorable associations for pooled beans. The separate insomnia analysis uses genetically proxied preferences. Canned black beans and Parkinson-related insomnia were not isolated.

fit: isolated DHA compared with placebo for Parkinson levodopa-induced dyskinesia
assessment: Preliminary poster found 3/15 versus 7/15 cases by 12 months with no reported peak-severity difference. The posted forceplate denominator differs. Neither contrast estimates walnut oil or alpha-linolenic acid.
